title: Move Zeroes
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, move all `0`s to the end of it while keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements.

You must do this **in place** without making a copy of the array. Return the array.

The order of the non-zero elements must not change — `[0,1,0,3,12]` becomes `[1,3,12,0,0]`, not `[3,1,12,0,0]`.

steps.caption: Both markers will start at the front — this pair moves at different speeds rather than from opposite ends.
slot starts at 0: the first position that still needs filling.
scan starts at 0 too, and it is the one that will visit every element.
nums[0] was a zero, so nothing was placed. scan moves on alone and slot stays waiting.
nums[scan] is 1, a non-zero, so it swaps into the slot — and the zero that was there gets pushed out to where scan is.
Only now does slot advance: position 0 is settled, so the next non-zero belongs at 1.
Another zero at index 2, so scan passes over it and slot holds its place again.
3 is non-zero, so it swaps down into the waiting slot.
12 swaps into the last waiting slot, and the zeros have been pushed to the back without ever being moved deliberately.
Every element has been scanned. Everything left of slot is settled, and the zeros fell to the end on their own.

checkpoints.question: scan just passed a zero and slot did not move. Why not?
options: slot only advances once something has actually been placed there
slot advances every time scan does, just one step behind
slot is waiting for scan to reach the end of the array
checkpoints.answer: slot only advances once something has actually been placed there
checkpoints.why: slot marks the first unfilled position. If it advanced past a zero, that zero would be treated as settled and would never reach the back.

checkpoints.question: A non-zero was just swapped into slot. What happens to slot now?
options: it advances, because that position is now settled
it stays, because the swap may need to be repeated
it jumps to wherever scan is
checkpoints.answer: it advances, because that position is now settled
checkpoints.why: The slot has been filled with the correct next value, so the boundary of the settled region moves forward by exactly one.

hints: The two markers here do not start at opposite ends. What if both start at the front and move at different speeds?
One marker scans every element. The other remembers the first position that still needs filling — it only advances when something is actually placed there.

Walk the whole array with a scanning index. Whenever the scanned value is non-zero, swap it into the slot position and advance the slot. Everything the slot has passed is settled, and the zeros fall to the back on their own.
